findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: The facility has written procedures for responding to a Norovirus event, however, there isn’t a chemical available to assist in cleaning. The PIC mentioned that the facility will purchase a bottle of bleach as soon as possible. Ensure that an EPA approved bleach is available to respond to a norovirus event. Will follow-up on October 20, 2026 to see that bleach has been purchased.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Garbage and refuse are properly disposed; facilities are maintained.
findings.comment: Trash was observed on the ground surrounding the outside dumpster. The dumpster lid was shut, however, there was discarded trash present on the ground. This can act as harboring conditions for rodents and insects. Ensure to educate employees on proper disposal of trash to prevent accumulation, as well as harboring conditions for unwanted pest.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.19(A) Storage Areas, Redeeming Machines, Receptacles and Waste Handling Units, Location. (A) An area designated for REFUSE, recyclables, returnables, and, except as specified in (B) of this section, a redeeming machine for recyclables or returnables shall be located so that it is separate from FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and a public health HAZARD or nuisance is not created.

findings.comment:

findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

An employee was observed to change gloves without washing hands. Education was conducted. Ensure that hand washing takes place at all times that hand washing is required when handling foods.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

The hand sink next to the three part sink has a small spray that comes out from the faucet when on. The PIC was aware of this and stated that the new area manager was planning on remedying the situation in the near future. Ensure that all plumbing in the facility is maintained in good repair at all times.

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
This is a repeat violaiton.

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Company is not showing on the list that inspector has for approved food handler courses from the State of Illinois. Every person working in a food service shall have their handler certification in basic food handling principles.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

Inspector observed a bottle of ranch dated 10/1 and a bottle of cool ranch dated 9/30 stored in the reach in portion of the make table. The items were discarded and the squeeze bottles placed at dish. Discussed with PIC throwing out food that has exceed the 7 day date marking rule. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Observed large parts of the walk-in cooler to have date marking missing. Some areas of the bottom prep cooler lacked date marking as well. Discussed with PIC. PIC indicated these items were prepped the night before or the day before that. PIC was actively date marking during the inspection to correct this violation. Ensure staff is aware of appropriate date marking system and disposal of foods within 7 day of prepared or thawed. COS.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no illness clean-up kit or policy with bleach procedures at the facility. Discussed purchasing a bodily fluid clean-up kit. Facility cannot use bleach. Inspector will follow-up on 3/29/21.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Observed fans of walk-in cooler to be dusty. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

(REPEAT) Observed caulk at three compartment sink to be no longer smooth and easily cleanable. Discussed repairs with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/13/2020.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-501.14: (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge. 

Observed hood above pizza oven to have a large accumulation of dust and debris. Discussed routine hood cleaning with PIC. Side of hood indicates Luxury Clean performs the service, but no date was listed.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

Observed no CFM present during spot check. Facility is aware that there must be a certified food manager available during all hours of operation. Discussed with PIC. Paperwork for courses has been left during the 1/13/20 inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

Observed PIC to wash hands improperly: turned off knob of sink before utilizing paper towels. A clean barrier must be used when turning off faucet and after properly washing hands. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(2) (Pf) PIC does not demonstrate the responsibility of preventing the transmission of foodborne disease by employees that may cause food borne disease. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(2).

Observed facility to have copies of employee health reporting agreements; however, no employees have signed the document. Discussed need for review with all employees regarding document and necessary signatures. Inspector will follow-up on 1/22/2020.

Observed unisex employee bathroom to lack a covered receptacle for disposal of feminine hygiene products. Discussed need for covered trash can with PIC.
